The IP transfers a stream of data words from a write clock domain to a read clock domain.
Words are read in the order in which they were written.

The two clocks may have different frequencies, but they are synchronous to each other: both derive from one source and keep a fixed phase relationship, for example 150 MHz and 100 MHz taken from one PLL (DEC-005).
Because the clocks are synchronous, the pointers cross from one domain to the other without synchronizers, as ordinary timed paths that static timing analysis (STA) closes.
The special case of two equal clocks (one clock) is a normal use.

The interface and the options are inherited from the sibling IP 001_AsyncGrayFIFO (DEC-002), without its clock-domain-crossing logic: write and read requests with full and empty flags, threshold flags, overflow and underflow pulses, a show-ahead read, a hardware reset per domain, and a software reset with a handshake.
Included:
Structural top m_vlsit_sfifo_top that instantiates the write module, the read module and the FIFO array module.
Write module (write clock domain): write pointer, full and full-threshold flags, overflow pulse, memory write port, software reset FSM for the write side.
Read module (read clock domain): read pointer, empty and empty-threshold flags, underflow pulse, memory read address, software reset FSM for the read side.
FIFO array module: a pure RTL array, or a library SRAM with one write port and one read port (replacement branch).
Any depth of 2 or more (not only a power of two), any data width of 1 bit or more.
One parameter that selects a direct pointer path or one retiming flop in the destination domain (PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME).
Gap-free streaming: with continuous write and continuous read there is only the initial latency and no gap (REQ-PERF-002).
Software reset with a four-phase handshake between the two domains.
Excluded:
Clock-domain crossing of unrelated (asynchronous) clocks; use 001_AsyncGrayFIFO for that case.
Software-visible registers (no CSR), interrupts, DFT structures, security and safety features, clock gating and power domains.
Data-integrity protection (ECC or parity).
Verification-only models and testbenches (they belong to the verification source set).

ID: REQ-FUNC-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: A write shall be accepted at a rising edge of i_clk_wr when i_wr_en is 1, writes are not blocked by the software reset, and o_full is 0. The word on i_wr_data at that edge shall be stored at the next free place.; Source: DEC-002, REF-001; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002; assertion SVA-001; waveform WF-001

ID: REQ-FUNC-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: A read shall be accepted at a rising edge of i_clk_rd when i_rd_en is 1, reads are not blocked by the software reset, and o_empty is 0. The word accepted is the word shown on o_rd_data before that edge. After an accepted read, o_rd_data shall show the next word (show-ahead) without a bubble when another word is stored.; Source: DEC-003; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002; assertion SVA-002; waveform WF-002

ID: REQ-FUNC-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: The words shall be read in the order in which they were written, with no loss and no duplication, for every legal depth, data width, clock ratio, PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME and memory option.; Source: DEC-002; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Scoreboard simulation: TEST-002, TEST-017

ID: REQ-FUNC-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: The FIFO shall store up to PARA_SFIFO_DEPTH words. o_full shall be 1 whenever PARA_SFIFO_DEPTH words are stored; it may be 1 while a place is free only because the freed place is not yet visible in the write domain (conservative flag). A write while o_full is 1 shall store nothing and leave the write pointer unchanged.; Source: DEC-013; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-003; assertion SVA-001, SVA-005; waveform WF-003

ID: REQ-FUNC-005; Requirement using shall/should/may: o_empty shall be 1 whenever no stored word is visible to the read side. o_empty may be 1 while a word exists only because the word is not yet visible in the read domain (conservative flag). o_rd_data shall be valid whenever o_empty is 0 and not meaningful while o_empty is 1. A read while o_empty is 1 shall leave the read pointer unchanged.; Source: DEC-013; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-004; assertion SVA-002, SVA-004; waveform WF-004

ID: REQ-FUNC-006; Requirement using shall/should/may: The depth shall be any integer of 2 or more. The pointers shall count modulo two times the depth, and the memory address shall be the pointer modulo the depth.; Source: DEC-004, DEC-015; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-008; waveform WF-012

ID: REQ-FUNC-007; Requirement using shall/should/may: o_full_thr shall be 1 when the occupancy seen by the write side is greater than or equal to i_full_thr. o_empty_thr shall be 1 when the occupancy seen by the read side is less than or equal to i_empty_thr. Both thresholds are static inputs.; Source: DEC-008; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-005; waveform WF-005

ID: REQ-FUNC-008; Requirement using shall/should/may: o_overflow shall be a pulse of one write-clock cycle in the cycle after a write was requested while o_full was 1 and writes were not blocked by the software reset. It is not sticky.; Source: DEC-008; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-003; assertion SVA-006; waveform WF-003

ID: REQ-FUNC-009; Requirement using shall/should/may: o_underflow shall be a pulse of one read-clock cycle in the cycle after a read was requested while o_empty was 1 and reads were not blocked by the software reset. It is not sticky.; Source: DEC-008; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-004; assertion SVA-007; waveform WF-004

ID: REQ-FUNC-010; Requirement using shall/should/may: A rejected write or read shall not change any pointer, any stored word, or the occupancy.; Source: DEC-002; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-003, TEST-004; assertion SVA-003

ID: REQ-IF-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall expose exactly the ports of Section 6.2. The port list shall not depend on a parameter value except for widths.; Source: REF-003 PRT-03; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Lint and port-list review: TEST-014

ID: REQ-IF-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: o_overflow, o_underflow, o_sw_rst_busy, o_full, o_full_thr, o_empty and o_empty_thr shall each be driven by a flip-flop, except that o_full, o_full_thr, o_empty and o_empty_thr shall be combined with the software reset block term by one gate (DEC-019). No other logic shall exist between these flip-flops and the ports.; Source: DEC-013, DEC-019; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Structural check of the RTL and the netlist: TEST-014

ID: REQ-IF-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: o_rd_data shall be the output register of the memory (read latency of one read-clock cycle) with no logic after it. It is not reset and not meaningful while o_empty is 1.; Source: DEC-003; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002; inspection: TEST-014

ID: REQ-CLK-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall operate with two clocks, i_clk_wr and i_clk_rd, of different or equal frequency, that are synchronous to each other: one source, a fixed phase relationship, any rational frequency ratio. Behavior shall be correct for every such ratio, including the case in which the two rising edges coincide.; Source: DEC-005; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation with several ratios: TEST-011, TEST-017

ID: REQ-CLK-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall contain no synchronizer and no clock-domain-crossing cell. Every path between the two domains shall be an ordinary timed path from a flip-flop of one domain to a flip-flop or the flag logic of the other, closed by STA with no false-path or asynchronous clock-group exception.; Source: DEC-005; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: STA review: TEST-015; structural check: TEST-014

ID: REQ-CLK-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: With PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 0 the pointer of the other domain shall enter the flag logic directly. With PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 1 it shall first be captured by one flip-flop in the destination domain. The parameter shall change only the latency of the flags and the timing of the crossing path, not the function.; Source: DEC-006; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-006; STA review: TEST-015

ID: REQ-RESET-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: Both resets i_rst_n_wr and i_rst_n_rd shall be active-low with asynchronous assertion. While asserted, every flip-flop of the domain shall be at its reset value: pointers 0, o_full 0, o_empty 1, o_overflow 0, o_underflow 0, both reset FSMs in RUN, o_sw_rst_busy 0, handshake flops 0.; Source: REF-003 RST-01; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Reset test: TEST-001

ID: REQ-RESET-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The release of each hardware reset shall be synchronous to the clock of its domain and shall be provided outside the IP. The two resets shall be asserted together. No operation shall start before both resets are released.; Source: DEC-007; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-001, TEST-011

ID: REQ-SRST-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: i_rst_n_sw = 0 in the write domain shall request a software reset. A low level of one cycle shall be enough; a longer low level shall be held until the sequence reaches its hold state.; Source: DEC-007, REF-001; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-009; waveform WF-013, WF-014

ID: REQ-SRST-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: From the cycle in which i_rst_n_sw is 0, writes shall be blocked with no clock delay (no flop in that path): o_full shall be 1, o_full_thr shall show the value of an empty FIFO, and no write shall be accepted. Writes remain blocked until o_sw_rst_busy is 0. A blocked write shall not raise o_overflow.; Source: DEC-007; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-009; assertion SVA-009

ID: REQ-SRST-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the request reaches the read side, reads shall be blocked: o_empty shall be 1, o_empty_thr shall be 1, and no read shall be accepted until the read side is released. A blocked read shall not raise o_underflow.; Source: DEC-007; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-009; assertion SVA-009

ID: REQ-SRST-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: The read side shall reset its pointer first and acknowledge; the write side shall then reset its pointer; the read side shall be released first and the write side last. The handshake shall be four-phase.; Source: DEC-007, REF-001; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-009; waveform WF-013

ID: REQ-SRST-005; Requirement using shall/should/may: At the end of a software reset sequence the FIFO shall be empty, both pointers shall be 0, and every stored word shall be discarded. The memory content shall not be erased.; Source: DEC-007; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-009

ID: REQ-SRST-006; Requirement using shall/should/may: o_sw_rst_busy shall be the output of a flip-flop. It shall be 1 from the cycle after the write FSM takes the request until the cycle in which the write FSM is back in RUN. The FIFO is ready for writes when o_sw_rst_busy is 0 and i_rst_n_sw is 1.; Source: DEC-007; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-009; assertion SVA-010

ID: REQ-SRST-007; Requirement using shall/should/may: A hardware reset shall have priority over a software reset at any time and shall bring both FSMs to RUN.; Source: DEC-007; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-010, TEST-011; waveform WF-015

ID: REQ-SRST-008; Requirement using shall/should/may: A request that arrives while a sequence is running (a low pulse in REL, or a second pulse) shall be served as a new sequence when the write FSM is back in RUN. A low level held in the hold state shall keep the sequence in the hold state.; Source: DEC-007; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-010

ID: REQ-PARAM-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall accept the parameter values listed in Section 8. The behavior with an illegal value is not specified and the IP does not check it (PAR-04 is not part of the rules).; Source: DEC-009; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Elaboration of the legal ranges: TEST-013

ID: REQ-PERF-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall accept one write per write-clock cycle and one read per read-clock cycle.; Source: DEC-012; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-007; waveform WF-008

ID: REQ-PERF-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: With i_wr_en and i_rd_en held at 1, there shall be only the initial latency and no gap: after the first word is available, every read-clock cycle in which the writer is not the limit accepts a read, and every write-clock cycle in which the reader is not the limit accepts a write. This is guaranteed when the depth is at least 4 + 2 x PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME. The side that runs at the higher clock frequency is held back by the other side only because of the rate difference.; Source: DEC-012; Applies to: All configurations with the stated depth; Verification method: Simulation and depth sweep: TEST-007; waveform WF-008 to WF-011

ID: REQ-PERF-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: After a write into an empty FIFO, o_empty shall fall after the first rising edge of i_clk_rd that is strictly later than the write edge (PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 0), or after the second such edge (PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 1). o_rd_data shall show the new word at that moment.; Source: DEC-013; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-006; waveform WF-001, WF-006, WF-007

ID: REQ-PERF-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: After a read from a full FIFO, o_full shall fall after the first rising edge of i_clk_wr that is strictly later than the read edge (PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 0), or after the second such edge (PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 1).; Source: DEC-013; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-006; waveform WF-006, WF-007

ID: REQ-PERF-005; Requirement using shall/should/may: The boundary flags shall be exact in their own domain with no extra latency: o_full shall be 1 in the cycle after the write that stores the last free place, and o_empty shall be 1 in the cycle after the read that takes the last word.; Source: DEC-013; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-003, TEST-004

ID: REQ-RTL-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The RTL shall comply with REF-003 and shall use the hierarchy of Section 14.2.; Source: REF-003; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Lint and rule check: TEST-014

ID: REQ-RTL-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The library SRAM shall be instantiated only inside a wrapper module of 000_Common (the cell VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R), with the instance name u_dont_touch_ followed by the function name (REF-003 NAM-09), and shall behave like the array branch from the point of view of Section 10.; Source: DEC-004; Applies to: CFG-MACRO; Verification method: Simulation with both branches: TEST-012; rule check: TEST-014

ID: REQ-RTL-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall contain no synchronizer module and no cell wrapper other than the SRAM wrapper. The retiming flop of PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME shall be a plain flip-flop of the RTL.; Source: DEC-005, DEC-006; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Inspection: TEST-014

ID: REQ-VER-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: Every waveform of the waveform plan (Section 10.3) shall exist as an image with its WaveJSON source, and the prototype scripts shall reproduce them.; Source: DEC-011; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: File check and rerun: TEST-016

ID: REQ-VER-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The scoreboard regression shall cover the depths 2, 3, 5, 8 and 12, both values of PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME, and several clock ratios including equal clocks, and shall report no error.; Source: DEC-005; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Regression: TEST-017

The IP has a write side in the write clock domain, a read side in the read clock domain, and a memory.
Each side owns one pointer (modulo two times the depth) and sees the pointer of the other side either directly or through one retiming flop.
The flags are flip-flops computed from the next pointer values (look-ahead), so each flag is exact at the edge of its own domain and conservative only by the visibility of the other side (DEC-013).

The frame is the top module, the blocks are its instances, each connector is one interface with its mnemonic, and the two tables under the diagram in the source file describe the blocks and the interfaces.*
Write.
The writer drives i_wr_en and i_wr_data.

At a rising edge of i_clk_wr with i_wr_en = 1 and o_full = 0 (and no software reset block) the word is stored at the address of the write pointer, the write pointer increments, and the flags are recomputed for the next cycle.
Visibility.
The new write pointer is a flop output of the write domain.
The read side uses it at its next rising edge that is strictly later (directly, or one edge later through the retiming flop).
The read flag register is loaded at that edge together with the memory output register, so the empty flag and the data change together.
Read.

At a rising edge of i_clk_rd with i_rd_en = 1 and o_empty = 0 the word shown on o_rd_data is taken, the read pointer increments, and the memory output register already loads the following word (the memory read address is the address of the next read pointer).
Release of a place.
The read pointer is visible to the write side at its next strictly later rising edge (directly, or one edge later), where o_full may fall.
The occupancy (write pointer minus read pointer, modulo two times the depth) is between 0 and PARA_SFIFO_DEPTH.
No write is accepted while o_full is 1, and no read is accepted while o_empty is 1.
o_full is 1 whenever the occupancy is PARA_SFIFO_DEPTH; o_empty is 1 whenever the occupancy is 0.
The write side never sees a read pointer that is ahead of the real one, and the read side never sees a write pointer that is ahead of the real one: the views only lag.
The memory read address always refers to the next read pointer, so the output register holds the word at the read pointer whenever o_empty is 0.
Pointers and flags change only at a rising edge of the clock of their own domain.

The FIFO interface follows these rules, the same on every configuration:
Request level.
A request (i_wr_en, i_rd_en) is a level sampled at every rising edge of its own clock.
It may be 1 for many cycles.
Each edge at which the request is 1 and the acceptance condition holds is one transaction.
There is no acknowledge handshake: the flag tells whether the request is accepted.
Write acceptance.
The write is accepted when i_wr_en = 1, o_full = 0 and writes are not blocked by the software reset.
A request is never accepted while o_full = 1.
Data does not need to be held after the accepting edge.
Read acceptance.
The read is accepted when i_rd_en = 1, o_empty = 0 and reads are not blocked. o_rd_data is the word to be taken and is valid for the whole cycle before the accepting edge.
Show-ahead.
After an accepted read, o_rd_data shows the next word in the next cycle, with no bubble, if another word is visible.
Flags are views. o_full and o_full_thr are the write view of the occupancy, o_empty and o_empty_thr the read view.
A view may lag the real occupancy in the direction that is safe (full late to fall, empty late to fall), never in the unsafe direction.
Rejected requests.
A rejected write or read changes nothing but raises the one-cycle overflow or underflow pulse.

A read of the address that is written at the same edge returns the old word; the flags make this harmless because the read side takes a word only after the flag fell, and the flag falls together with the output register that holds the new word (Section 5.3).

Reading the old word during a collision is part of the contract of the memory model of 000_Common.

The occupancy is occ(a, b) = a - b if a is not below b, otherwise a + 2 x DEPTH - b.

The sequence resets both pointers safely.
It is the handshake of the sibling IP with the synchronizers replaced by the timed crossing of PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME (DEC-017).
Request.
The controller drives i_rst_n_sw to 0 in the write domain.
From that cycle writes are blocked (no flop in the path) and o_full is 1.
The write FSM leaves RUN, o_sw_rst_busy rises in the next cycle, and the request flop is raised.
Read side.
The read FSM sees the request, blocks reads (o_empty = 1), resets the read pointer (state RST, one cycle) and raises the acknowledge.
Write side.
The write FSM sees the acknowledge, resets the write pointer (state PTR, one cycle) and waits in HOLD until i_rst_n_sw is 1.
Release.
In REL the request is dropped.
The read side leaves ACK first, when it sees the request at 0 and the write pointer at 0 (flush check).
The write side leaves REL when it sees the acknowledge at 0 and the read pointer at 0, then returns to RUN; o_sw_rst_busy falls.
The FIFO is ready for writes when o_sw_rst_busy is 0 and i_rst_n_sw is 1.
A one-cycle low pulse starts the complete sequence.
A hardware reset at any step clears all FSMs.
A new low level during REL is served after the write FSM is back in RUN.

Term / acronym: Synchronous clocks; Definition: Two clocks derived from one source with a fixed phase relationship, possibly of different frequency
Term / acronym: Timed path; Definition: A path between flops of two related clocks that STA closes at the nearest launch and capture edges
Term / acronym: Occupancy; Definition: Number of words stored: write pointer minus read pointer, modulo two times the depth
Term / acronym: View; Definition: The occupancy as seen by one side, using the pointer of the other side that may lag
Term / acronym: Show-ahead; Definition: The read data already shows the word at the read pointer before the read request
Term / acronym: Look-ahead flag; Definition: A flag flop loaded from the next pointer values
Term / acronym: Gap-free streaming; Definition: After the initial latency, one word accepted in every clock cycle of the side that is not limited by the clock ratio
Term / acronym: PTR_RETIME; Definition: The parameter that adds one retiming flop to the pointers and handshake signals that cross to another domain
Term / acronym: Block term; Definition: Software reset block of a side: busy flop or i_rst_n_sw low (write), request seen or FSM not in RUN (read)
Term / acronym: FSM; Definition: Finite-state machine
Term / acronym: SRAM macro; Definition: A library memory with one write port and one read port behind a wrapper

Write interface and read interface of a FIFO

A write shall be accepted at a rising edge of i_clk_wr when i_wr_en is 1, writes are not blocked by the software reset, and o_full is 0. The word on i_wr_data at that edge shall be stored at the next free place.
Simulation: TEST-002; assertion SVA-001; waveform WF-001

A read shall be accepted at a rising edge of i_clk_rd when i_rd_en is 1, reads are not blocked by the software reset, and o_empty is 0. The word accepted is the word shown on o_rd_data before that edge. After an accepted read, o_rd_data shall show the next word (show-ahead) without a bubble when another word is stored.
Simulation: TEST-002; assertion SVA-002; waveform WF-002
The words shall be read in the order in which they were written, with no loss and no duplication, for every legal depth, data width, clock ratio, PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME and memory option.

The FIFO shall store up to PARA_SFIFO_DEPTH words. o_full shall be 1 whenever PARA_SFIFO_DEPTH words are stored; it may be 1 while a place is free only because the freed place is not yet visible in the write domain (conservative flag). A write while o_full is 1 shall store nothing and leave the write pointer unchanged.
Simulation: TEST-003; assertion SVA-001, SVA-005; waveform WF-003

o_empty shall be 1 whenever no stored word is visible to the read side. o_empty may be 1 while a word exists only because the word is not yet visible in the read domain (conservative flag). o_rd_data shall be valid whenever o_empty is 0 and not meaningful while o_empty is 1. A read while o_empty is 1 shall leave the read pointer unchanged.
Simulation: TEST-004; assertion SVA-002, SVA-004; waveform WF-004
The depth shall be any integer of 2 or more. The pointers shall count modulo two times the depth, and the memory address shall be the pointer modulo the depth.

o_full_thr shall be 1 when the occupancy seen by the write side is greater than or equal to i_full_thr. o_empty_thr shall be 1 when the occupancy seen by the read side is less than or equal to i_empty_thr. Both thresholds are static inputs.
o_overflow shall be a pulse of one write-clock cycle in the cycle after a write was requested while o_full was 1 and writes were not blocked by the software reset. It is not sticky.
Simulation: TEST-003; assertion SVA-006; waveform WF-003
o_underflow shall be a pulse of one read-clock cycle in the cycle after a read was requested while o_empty was 1 and reads were not blocked by the software reset. It is not sticky.
Simulation: TEST-004; assertion SVA-007; waveform WF-004
A rejected write or read shall not change any pointer, any stored word, or the occupancy.
The IP shall expose exactly the ports of Section 6.2. The port list shall not depend on a parameter value except for widths.

o_overflow, o_underflow, o_sw_rst_busy, o_full, o_full_thr, o_empty and o_empty_thr shall each be driven by a flip-flop, except that o_full, o_full_thr, o_empty and o_empty_thr shall be combined with the software reset block term by one gate (DEC-019). No other logic shall exist between these flip-flops and the ports.
Structural check of the RTL and the netlist: TEST-014
o_rd_data shall be the output register of the memory (read latency of one read-clock cycle) with no logic after it. It is not reset and not meaningful while o_empty is 1.

The IP shall operate with two clocks, i_clk_wr and i_clk_rd, of different or equal frequency, that are synchronous to each other: one source, a fixed phase relationship, any rational frequency ratio. Behavior shall be correct for every such ratio, including the case in which the two rising edges coincide.
Simulation with several ratios: TEST-011, TEST-017

The IP shall contain no synchronizer and no clock-domain-crossing cell. Every path between the two domains shall be an ordinary timed path from a flip-flop of one domain to a flip-flop or the flag logic of the other, closed by STA with no false-path or asynchronous clock-group exception.
STA review: TEST-015; structural check: TEST-014

With PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 0 the pointer of the other domain shall enter the flag logic directly. With PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 1 it shall first be captured by one flip-flop in the destination domain. The parameter shall change only the latency of the flags and the timing of the crossing path, not the function.

Both resets i_rst_n_wr and i_rst_n_rd shall be active-low with asynchronous assertion. While asserted, every flip-flop of the domain shall be at its reset value: pointers 0, o_full 0, o_empty 1, o_overflow 0, o_underflow 0, both reset FSMs in RUN, o_sw_rst_busy 0, handshake flops 0.

The release of each hardware reset shall be synchronous to the clock of its domain and shall be provided outside the IP. The two resets shall be asserted together. No operation shall start before both resets are released.
i_rst_n_sw = 0 in the write domain shall request a software reset. A low level of one cycle shall be enough; a longer low level shall be held until the sequence reaches its hold state.

From the cycle in which i_rst_n_sw is 0, writes shall be blocked with no clock delay (no flop in that path): o_full shall be 1, o_full_thr shall show the value of an empty FIFO, and no write shall be accepted. Writes remain blocked until o_sw_rst_busy is 0. A blocked write shall not raise o_overflow.

When the request reaches the read side, reads shall be blocked: o_empty shall be 1, o_empty_thr shall be 1, and no read shall be accepted until the read side is released. A blocked read shall not raise o_underflow.

The read side shall reset its pointer first and acknowledge; the write side shall then reset its pointer; the read side shall be released first and the write side last. The handshake shall be four-phase.
At the end of a software reset sequence the FIFO shall be empty, both pointers shall be 0, and every stored word shall be discarded. The memory content shall not be erased.

o_sw_rst_busy shall be the output of a flip-flop. It shall be 1 from the cycle after the write FSM takes the request until the cycle in which the write FSM is back in RUN. The FIFO is ready for writes when o_sw_rst_busy is 0 and i_rst_n_sw is 1.
A hardware reset shall have priority over a software reset at any time and shall bring both FSMs to RUN.

A request that arrives while a sequence is running (a low pulse in REL, or a second pulse) shall be served as a new sequence when the write FSM is back in RUN. A low level held in the hold state shall keep the sequence in the hold state.
The IP shall accept the parameter values listed in Section 8. The behavior with an illegal value is not specified and the IP does not check it (PAR-04 is not part of the rules).
Elaboration of the legal ranges: TEST-013
The IP shall accept one write per write-clock cycle and one read per read-clock cycle.

With i_wr_en and i_rd_en held at 1, there shall be only the initial latency and no gap: after the first word is available, every read-clock cycle in which the writer is not the limit accepts a read, and every write-clock cycle in which the reader is not the limit accepts a write. This is guaranteed when the depth is at least 4 + 2 x PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME. The side that runs at the higher clock frequency is held back by the other side only because of the rate difference.
All configurations with the stated depth
Simulation and depth sweep: TEST-007; waveform WF-008 to WF-011

After a write into an empty FIFO, o_empty shall fall after the first rising edge of i_clk_rd that is strictly later than the write edge (PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 0), or after the second such edge (PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 1). o_rd_data shall show the new word at that moment.
Simulation: TEST-006; waveform WF-001, WF-006, WF-007

After a read from a full FIFO, o_full shall fall after the first rising edge of i_clk_wr that is strictly later than the read edge (PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 0), or after the second such edge (PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME = 1).

The boundary flags shall be exact in their own domain with no extra latency: o_full shall be 1 in the cycle after the write that stores the last free place, and o_empty shall be 1 in the cycle after the read that takes the last word.
The RTL shall comply with REF-003 and shall use the hierarchy of Section 14.2.

The library SRAM shall be instantiated only inside a wrapper module of 000_Common (the cell VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R), with the instance name u_dont_touch_ followed by the function name (REF-003 NAM-09), and shall behave like the array branch from the point of view of Section 10.
Simulation with both branches: TEST-012; rule check: TEST-014
The IP shall contain no synchronizer module and no cell wrapper other than the SRAM wrapper. The retiming flop of PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME shall be a plain flip-flop of the RTL.
Every waveform of the waveform plan (Section 10.3) shall exist as an image with its WaveJSON source, and the prototype scripts shall reproduce them.
The scoreboard regression shall cover the depths 2, 3, 5, 8 and 12, both values of PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME, and several clock ratios including equal clocks, and shall report no error.
